This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. Major organizations including Apple
and the National Security Agency reported more computer outages today, and NPR's Greg Miring
has the latest. Apple users reported problems with both the App Store and Apple Pay. At the
National Security Agency, the nation's largest intelligence agency, an internal communications
network went down. The agency said this happened during scheduled routine maintenance, adding that
"mission-critical capabilities" were not affected. These are the latest in a series of seemingly
unrelated computer outages in recent days. They've included Microsoft, major banks, and the Federal
Aviation Administration. Computer experts say there's no indication these organizations have
been hacked. Rather, they say, the computer networks appear to be going down as they are
being patched or upgraded. Greg Miring, NPR News, Washington.
NVIDIA's board does not intend to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang. This comes just days
after Huang stepped down after it came to light that he'd had an affair with a woman who may have
been recruited to spy for China, and PR's John Ruich has more. There has been a groundswell of
support for Jensen Huang, with backers saying allegations against him have not yet been fully
investigated and he should not have had to leave the company he founded. This week, Huang broke
days of silence to say he would return to the company if the board thought it was the right move.
But board chairman Harvey Jones poured cold water on that idea. The NVIDIA board unanimously
accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO. Interim CEO Collette
Kress said NVIDIA's ambitions won't change going forward. John Ruich, NPR News. House Democratic
leader Hakeem Jeffries today endorsed lowering the age for people to become eligible for Medicare
and adding benefits and universal coverage for kids. We should expand coverage to include
vision, hearing, and dental, and we should cover all the kids in the United States of America.
Right? Those are bold actions, meaningful actions, important actions that can be taken
on our march toward universal health coverage. Jeffries didn't say what age people should
become eligible for Medicare. The federal health insurance program for people age 65 or older and
younger people with disabilities. But first, Jeffries said when Democrats retake control of Congress,
they should reverse Medicaid cuts enacted by President Trump's tax and policy bill
and restore Affordable Care Act tax credits that expired last year.
Iran fired drones at a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain today. The move was Iran's third attack
on American military targets in the kingdom in recent days after a two-month lull. The attacks
come as the USS Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group arrived in the region to expand
U.S. military firepower amid the nearly nine-month war. The U.S. stock market dropped again today.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Ukrainian drones and missiles struck the vital Kerch bridge linking Russia to the occupied
Crimean Peninsula. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the operation unprecedented.
Russia's top criminal investigation agency acknowledged that the bridge was attacked and
damaged but didn't elaborate. The Iran war has pushed up oil prices. The Alaska desk's Shelby
Herbert reports it means Alaskans who rely on diesel to heat their homes will have to pay more
to survive winter temperatures. At her wit's end with her monthly heating bill, over a grand,
one Fairbanks president works on her house in about a foot of snow wielding a crowbar.
Moana Stubber is tearing off the aluminum exterior of her historic home to install
modern foam insulation panels to trap more heat so she can burn less oil. But she says many of
her friends and neighbors haven't been so lucky. I know at least a dozen people that have moved.
Folks that have lived year-round for ages. And then there are rural communities that aren't
connected to the state's highway system. Oil gets delivered just a few times a year by plane or
barge. Economists at the Alaska Center for Energy and Power say for those who didn't get their
delivery before the war, the worst may be yet to come. For NPR News, I'm Shelby Herbert in Fairbanks,
Alaska. Golfer Tiger Woods will return to competition in two weeks in the Bahamas. Woods
has announced that he'll be part of the 20-man field at the Hero World Challenge in December.
He last competed in the 2024 British Open in March this year. He was arrested and jailed on
a DUI charge in Florida. This is NPR News. Support for this podcast and the following
